seo.metaTitle: Tustin Workplace Injury Help | Free Case Review
seo.metaDescription: Hurt on the job in Tustin? Get a free case review to understand your workers' comp and third-party claim options.

hero.subtitle: Whether you were hurt in a warehouse off I-5, on a Jamboree Road job site, or behind the wheel for work on Red Hill Avenue, a Tustin workplace injury can involve more than one claim. We can explain which ones apply to you, at no cost.

about.title: Tustin Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Tustin's workforce is spread across distribution yards near I-5, medical and office campuses along Jamboree Road, retail and restaurant jobs on Newport Avenue, and light industry and auto shops off Red Hill Avenue. An injury in any of those settings usually begins with a workers' compensation claim. Under California law, that system is normally your only remedy against your own employer, and it pays regardless of who was at fault. It does not, however, close the door on everyone else. If a subcontractor, a property owner, the maker of a defective machine, or another driver caused your injury, a separate claim against that third party may be available, and it carries its own two-year deadline. Driving for work matters here as well: Tustin's public record for 2025 lists 328 injury collisions and 441 people injured citywide, many along the same corridors employees travel every shift. We handle workplace injury and third-party claims in Orange County and can help you understand which paths fit your situation.

about.ctaText: Tell us what happened and we'll review your case, free.

items.title: Two Systems, Explained Plainly
items.desc: Workers' compensation covers you against your employer regardless of fault, but a negligent third party can be held to a separate standard. We can review whether both apply to your Tustin injury.

items.title: Deadlines Kept in View
items.desc: California expects you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and third-party injury claims generally must be filed within two years. Reaching out early keeps those windows open.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: Firing, demoting, or punishing a worker for reporting an injury is illegal in California. We can help you document what happened if your employer pushes back.

items.question: I was hit on Red Hill Avenue while making deliveries for my job. Is that just a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were working, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages no matter who caused the crash. If another driver was at fault, you may also have a separate injury claim against that driver, and it follows California's two-year deadline. We can review the collision report and explain how the two claims interact.

items.question: Can my Tustin employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No. California law prohibits retaliation against an employee for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' compensation claim. Report the injury to your employer within 30 days, keep copies of everything you submit, and note any change in your hours, duties, or treatment afterward. If something feels off, we can advise on your options.

items.question: Do you charge me anything for a case review?
items.answer: No. We offer a free case review to injured people in Tustin and throughout Orange County. We handle injury claims on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery.
